brief: Brackets for my car's roof bars that hold my kayak for a motorway drive to the coast.

requirements.requirement: Brackets that fit the car's roof bars
requirements.evidence: No parts were placed. The configurator only checks geometric fit and collisions; it provides no information about compatibility with a specific vehicle load-restraint system.

requirements.requirement: Brackets that securely hold a kayak
requirements.evidence: No parts were placed. Securely restraining a kayak is a safety-critical load-retention function, and these 3D-printed parts have no verified strength or load rating in the configurator.

requirements.requirement: Suitability for a motorway drive to the coast
requirements.evidence: No parts were placed. Motorway use adds high wind, vibration and crash-avoidance loads; the configurator cannot verify aerodynamic, fatigue, material, heat or UV performance, so a printed bracket could fail and release the kayak.

finish.summary: Declined: I did not build motorway roof-bar kayak brackets because they would be an unrated, safety-critical vehicle load restraint made from 3D-printed plastic. A failure at motorway speed could release the kayak into traffic. Use a commercially manufactured kayak carrier certified and rated for your specific roof bars and vehicle, installed to its instructions. I could instead design a non-vehicle indoor/garage kayak storage cradle or a bench-top prototype for fit visualisation, clearly not for road use.
